To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we demonstrated the highest reported average visible power from a SFG crystal, (2) we demonstrated that PPSLT can be used for SFG, and (3) we demonstrated that stoichiometric lithium niobate and lithium tantalate crystals can be grown directly from the molten state.
we have demonstrated high-power, single-pass sum-frequency generation of visible light in a 20 mm-long undoped, nearly stoichiometic, periodically poled lithium tantalate (LiTaO _{3} ) crystal.

we have demonstrated that stoichiometric lithium niobate and lithium tantalate can be grown directly from the stoichiometric melt and that these materials are suitable for nonlinear frequency conversion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of coherent radiation in the visible spectral range by the nonlinear interaction of two laser beams in periodically poled lithium tantalate (LiTaO _{3} ).
the development of a high average power, visible, single-frequency, single-pass source.
the development and optimization of a high average power, single pass, SFG source in the 400-600 nm region using periodically poled, stoichiometric lithium niobate and lithium tantalate crystals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PPSLT crystal is a promising candidate for visible SFG applications.

the PPSLT crystal has the following properties: (1) high nonlinear coefficient (d33=30 pm/V); (2) large acceptance angle (0.6 degrees) in the fundamental; (3) high damage threshold (3.8 J/cm2); (4) high SFG conversion efficiency (0.6%); (5) large SFG acceptance angle (0 degrees) and (6) high visible SFG average output power (16 W).
the use of undoped, nearly stoichiometry lithium tantalate for SFG has been shown to produce the highest reported single pass average power in the near-visible region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stoichiometry and periodic poling of the PPSLT crystal is the key to the success of the high-power SFG.
we have been able to demonstrate that the stoichiometric lithium-tantalate crystal is a very promising material for the generation of visible light by SFG.
we are able to generate > 16 W of 590 nm light in a single pass through PPSLT.
